1. Reproduce it yourself on the matching surface via the control skill (Non-negotiables). Don't hand the repro to the user. A debug or instrumentation protocol that says to ask the user does not override this; you drive the instrumented runtime. Ask the user only with a stated, specific reason the control surface cannot reach the target, and only after driving it as far as it goes. Won't reproduce directly, force it: synthesize the trigger, tighten conditions, or instrument until it fires. A bug you can't reproduce, you can't prove fixed.

decisions.decision: Validate manifests, CLI input, paths, hashes, and recovery only at their owning seams.
Build one dry-run cleanup command and verifier instead of editing the repository by hand.
Replace repeated file laws with registry validation, denial checks, and the test dispatcher.
Use architect and arena before accepting replay, analysis, or corpus interface changes.
Leave the next agent one START_HERE path and the maintainer one owner per fact.

decisions.decision: Land protection, liveness shapes, and complete verification before deletion.
Work phase by phase and delegate bounded, disjoint tasks.
Prefer proven deletion, consolidation, and existing interfaces over new layers.
Make audit, move, deduplicate, and delete operations dry-runnable and convergent.
Move every caller, test, build rule, and pointer with each removed path or interface.
Contract the root, remove pass-throughs, and give every fact one canonical home.
Encode liveness, semantic role, recovery, action, and state in typed registry rows.
Proceed with reversible verified work and pause only before an unmanifested delete or external write.
Converge on the target tree without permanent redirects, dual interfaces, or an archive root.
Bind every destructive unit to a recovery, rebuild, identity, or semantic oracle.
Separate current state, stable rules, chronology, machine authority, data, and evidence.
Give workers disjoint write ownership and keep destructive phases under one registry writer.
Execute eleven ordered phases and keep every completed unit green.
Remove proven safe waste before path moves, module reshaping, and documentation polish.
Use enums and typed rows for liveness states, actions, recovery classes, and interfaces.
Use module, interface, seam, adapter, depth, leverage, and locality consistently.
Keep replay, analysis, corpus, and dispatch interfaces smaller than hidden knowledge.
Apply the deletion test and real-adapter rule before keeping an abstraction.
Accept dependencies and test behavior through each module interface.
Place interfaces at seams that concentrate changing knowledge.
Reject line-count depth, transport-type interfaces, and overloaded boundary terminology.
Classify dependencies and replace shallow tests with interface tests.
Classify redesigned dependencies before choosing adapters.
Expose seams only when real production and test implementations justify them.
Delete retired internal tests after replacement interface tests pass.
Compare at least two distinct interfaces for each deepening candidate.
Write behavior tests through public interfaces with independent expected values.
Test the approved cleanup CLI, registry, dispatcher, replay, corpus, and root seams.
Reject private tests, internal mocks, tautologies, and horizontal test batches.
Run one failing behavior test, one minimal implementation, and one green proof per slice.
Keep expected values independent and tests stable across internal refactors.
Use named fakes only for filesystem, recovery, time, and true external seams.
Use sharp START_HERE pointers and keep branch facts out of always-loaded prose.
Reduce agent context load and maintainer document-choice load.
Keep current steps, stable rules, chronology, and exact authority in separate owners.
Give each retained agent document a checkable purpose and deletion criterion.
Split reference only when a real branch earns a pointer.
Use liveness, authority, recovery, and chronology as stable terms.
Delete cached facts, duplicate meaning, stale branches, and no-op instructions.
Run narrow tests throughout and the complete registry at the end.
Keep touched functions focused, files below 500 lines, names specific, and types explicit.
Preserve intent comments and remove narration introduced by this work.
Give new behavior independent tests and keep one complete project command.
Inject external dependencies and hide third-party details behind owned interfaces.
Use predictable paths and split modules by owned knowledge.
Run each language default formatter over touched production files.
Keep diagnostic logs structured and CLI output plain.
